book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 52 · Rescue Awareness and Operations
title: Confined Spaces, Water and Wilderness: Care in Long Rescues

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already treat hypothermia, ventilate drowning patients and restrict spinal motion. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize confined space and trench dangers, and stay out
  2. Water and ice: reach, throw, row, go, cold water, the spine
  3. Long rescues: crush, cold, packaging, and what the PCP adds

Textbook: Chapter 52, PDF pages 4313–4340 (Additional Specialized Rescue Situations, Prehospital Care)
slides.say: Welcome back. Today we finish Chapter 52 with rescues where the hazard can easily take the rescuer too: confined spaces, trenches, water and ice, rope and wilderness. As EMRs, you already treat hypothermia, ventilate drowning patients and restrict spinal motion. As a PCP, two things change. You'll often be the first trained person there, so recognizing the danger and staying out is part of your clinical judgment. And these rescues are long, so your new tools, IV access, positive pressure and fluid boluses, must be planned around crush injury, cold and difficult packaging. Let's start below ground.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天把第 52 章讲完，讲那些危险很容易连救援者一起吞掉的救援：密闭空间、沟渠、水域和冰面、绳索和野外。作为 EMR，你已经会处理低体温、给溺水病人通气、限制脊柱活动。作为 PCP，有两点变化：你常常是第一个到场的受训人员，所以识别危险、不贸然进入，本身就是临床判断的一部分；而且这些救援耗时很长，你的新工具，静脉通路、正压通气和补液，都要围绕挤压伤、寒冷和困难的包装来计划。先从地下说起。

slides.title: Confined spaces: assume the air can kill
slides.body:
Of confined-space deaths, 60% are rescuers

  • Not built for people; few ways in or out: tanks, silos, septic tanks
  • Low oxygen, toxic or flammable gas, engulfing grain, machinery
  • Often dispatched as a heart attack or sudden illness
  • Assume an IDLH atmosphere; don't go in
  • Secure the scene, keep everyone out, brief the rescue team
slides.say: A confined space isn't designed for people to stay in and has few ways in or out: tanks, silos, pits, sewers, septic tanks, even a car trunk. The air may lack oxygen or hold toxic or flammable gas; grain can swallow a person like quicksand; and switched-off machinery can still hold stored energy. Remember this number: sixty percent of confined-space deaths are rescuers. These calls are often dispatched as a heart attack, because the caller only saw someone collapse. Assume the air is IDLH, meaning immediately dangerous to life and health. Don't go in. Secure the scene, keep everyone out, question witnesses, and brief the technical team.
slides.sayZh: 密闭空间不供人持续停留、进出口很少：储罐、筒仓、坑、下水道、化粪池，甚至汽车后备箱。里面的空气可能缺氧，或含有有毒、易燃气体；粮食会像流沙一样把人吞没；关掉的机器仍可能储存着能量。记住这个数字：密闭空间事故的死者中，百分之六十是救援者。这类呼叫常被派成「心脏病发作」，因为报警人只看到有人倒下。要假定里面的空气是 IDLH，也就是「立即威胁生命和健康」。不要进去。控制现场，不让任何人进入，询问目击者，并向专业队做简报。

slides.title: Gases your nose can't judge
slides.body:
GasKey fact
Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S)heavier than air; soon deadens smell
Carbon monoxide (CO)no smell; binds hemoglobin 200–250× more than O₂
Carbon dioxide (CO₂)asphyxiant; sour taste, stinging nose
Methanenot toxic, but explodes long before it suffocates
Ammonialighter than air; collects at the top

Only an air monitor can say the air is safe.
slides.say: Hydrogen sulphide comes from rotting organic matter in sewers, swamps and standing water. It's heavier than air, so it sinks, and it smells strong at first but quickly deadens your sense of smell, so losing the smell doesn't mean it's gone. Carbon monoxide has no smell, and hemoglobin grabs it two hundred to two hundred fifty times more strongly than oxygen. Carbon dioxide displaces oxygen. Methane, from sewage and manure, isn't toxic, but it explodes at levels far below what would suffocate you. Ammonia, from farm fertilizer, is lighter than air and collects at the top. Only an air monitor can say the air is safe.
slides.sayZh: 硫化氢来自下水道、沼泽和积水中腐烂的有机物，比空气重，会沉到底部；起初气味很冲，但很快就麻痹嗅觉，所以闻不到了不代表它没了。一氧化碳完全没有气味，血红蛋白和它结合的能力是氧的两百到两百五十倍。二氧化碳会把氧气挤走。甲烷来自污水和粪肥，本身没毒，但在远低于致人窒息的浓度时就会爆炸。氨来自农用化肥，比空气轻，聚在顶部。只有空气检测仪才能判断空气是否安全。

slides.title: Trench collapse
slides.body:
• Most collapses: trenches under 4 m deep and 2 m wide
  • Buried in heavy soil → asphyxia; can't just be pulled out
  • Second collapse: vibration, people at the edge, water
  • Keep everyone back; shut down machinery; stop or divert traffic
  • Talk to the victim; approach only from the narrow end, if you must
  • No entry until the team has put in shoring
slides.say: Most trench collapses happen in trenches less than four metres deep and two metres wide, so they don't look dangerous. But soil is heavy. A buried worker asphyxiates, and a partly buried person can't simply be pulled out; they're dug out after the team has shored, meaning braced, the walls. The biggest risk is a second collapse, set off by vibration, people at the edge, or water washing the soil away. So keep everyone back from the edge, shut down heavy machinery, and stop or divert nearby traffic. Talk to the trapped person if it's safe. If you must approach, come from the narrow end, where the soil is more stable.
slides.sayZh: 大多数沟渠坍塌发生在深不到四米、宽不到两米的沟里，所以看起来并不危险。但土很重：被埋的工人会窒息，被埋了一部分的人也不能硬拉出来，要等救援队把沟壁支护好、也就是撑住之后再挖出来。最大的风险是二次坍塌，振动、有人站在沟边、水把土冲走都可能引发。所以让所有人远离沟边，关停重型机械，截停或改道附近交通。安全的话，和被困者喊话。如果必须靠近，从窄的一端过去，那里土更稳。

slides.q: Dispatch: a worker collapsed in a sewer access hole, possible heart attack. On arrival, a coworker says a second worker climbed down to help and also collapsed. What do you do?
options: Climb down quickly with oxygen, since time matters
Lower your partner on a rope while you hold it
Keep everyone out, treat the air as IDLH, call the technical rescue team
Shout down, and go in if no one answers
slides.say: Let's check your judgment. Dispatch says a worker collapsed in a sewer access hole, possibly a heart attack. When you arrive, a coworker tells you a second worker climbed down to help and also collapsed. What do you do? A, climb down quickly with oxygen, since time matters. B, lower your partner on a rope while you hold it. C, keep everyone out, treat the air as IDLH, and call the technical rescue team. D, shout down, and go in if no one answers. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检验一下你的判断。调度说一名工人在下水道检修井里倒下，可能是心脏病。你到场后，一名工友说另一个工人下去救人，也倒下了。你怎么做？A 带上氧气赶快下去，时间要紧；B 用绳子把搭档放下去，你在上面拉着；C 不让任何人进入，按 IDLH 环境处理，呼叫专业技术救援队；D 往下喊话，没人回答就下去。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. A second collapse is the classic sign of a deadly atmosphere, and most people who die in confined spaces are would-be rescuers. This needs a team with air monitors and breathing apparatus. A and D put you in the same air that dropped two workers, and B does the same to your partner. Your job is to recognize the danger, secure the scene, gather information and brief the team when it arrives.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。第二个人也倒下，是致命空气的典型信号；密闭空间事故的死者大多是想去救人的人。这需要带空气检测仪和呼吸器的专业队。A 和 D 让你吸入放倒两名工人的同样的空气，B 则让你的搭档去冒同样的险。你的任务是识别危险、控制现场、收集信息，并在专业队到场时向他们做简报。

slides.title: Cold water: minutes count
slides.body:
• Water removes heat 25 times faster than air
  • In 4 °C water, death is likely after 15–20 minutes
  • HELP position (needs a PFD) cuts heat loss about 60%
  • Below 21 °C, cold may protect the brain: keep resuscitating
  • Lift out horizontally: cold diuresis leaves them low on fluid
  • Limit exertion: a cold heart is prone to arrhythmias
slides.say: Cold water kills fast. Water pulls heat from the body twenty-five times faster than air; in water around four degrees, death is likely within fifteen to twenty minutes. Someone wearing a PFD, a personal flotation device, can use the HELP position: knees to chest, arms tight to the sides, head out of the water, cutting heat loss by about sixty percent compared with treading water. Cold can also protect: below about twenty-one degrees, cooling may shield the brain from lack of oxygen, so keep resuscitating and transport. Lift cold patients out horizontally; cold diuresis, extra urine from the cold, leaves them low on fluid. Limit their exertion.
slides.sayZh: 冷水杀人很快。水带走体热的速度是空气的二十五倍；在四度左右的水里，人可能十五到二十分钟就会死亡。穿着 PFD（个人漂浮装置）的人可以采用 HELP 姿势：屈膝贴胸、双臂夹紧身体两侧、头露出水面，和踩水相比能减少约百分之六十的散热。寒冷也能起保护作用：在低于约二十一度的水里，降温可能保护大脑免于缺氧，所以要持续复苏并转运。把低体温病人从水里抬出来时要保持水平：冷利尿，也就是寒冷导致尿量增多，会让他们体液不足。还要尽量减少他们用力。

slides.title: Water and ice: reach, throw, row, go
slides.body:
Reach→Throw→Row→Go
  • PFD for anyone within 3 m of the water
  • Throw bag: tell them to grab the rope, not the bag
  • Still-water lifeguard ≠ ready for swift water
  • Low-head dams, strainers, flooded roads: deadly for rescuers
  • Ice: ropes, flotation, ladders to spread weight; trained teams
slides.say: Don't jump in after someone struggling in water. Use reach, throw, row, go. Reach with a branch, pole or paddle. If that's too short, throw a life buoy or throw bag, and tell the person to grab the rope, not the bag. Row out only if you can handle the boat and you're wearing a PFD. Go into the water only as a last resort, and only if you're trained. Anyone within three metres of the water needs a PFD. Moving water is deadly: low-head dams pull people under again and again, and strainers like fallen trees trap them. On ice, trained teams use ropes, flotation and ladders.
slides.sayZh: 看到有人在水里挣扎，不要跳下去。按「伸、抛、划、游」来。先伸：用树枝、杆子或桨去够。够不着就抛：抛救生圈或抛绳袋，告诉对方抓绳子、别抓袋子。只有会驾船并穿着 PFD 时才划船过去。下水是最后手段，而且只有受过训练才可以。在水边三米以内的人都要穿 PFD。流动的水非常危险：低水头坝会把人一次又一次卷入水下，倒下的树这类「滤网物」会把人卡住。冰面救援由受过训练的队伍用绳索、漂浮物和梯子进行。

slides.title: Spinal injury in the water
slides.body:
• Suspect: diving or fall, unknown mechanism, weak or numb limbs
  1. Turn face up by rolling the upper body as a unit
  2. Ventilate right away if needed, still in the water
  3. Float a backboard under; secure torso, then head
  4. Lift out on the board; remove wet clothes, cover
slides.say: Suspect a spinal injury in the water after a dive or fall, when an unresponsive patient's neck injury can't be ruled out, with weakness, numbness or paralysis, or whenever you're unsure. Diving injuries usually hit the neck, so the spine is stabilized before leaving the water. Rescuers turn a face-down patient face up by rotating the whole upper body together, not just the head. Breathing comes first: once face up, open the airway and ventilate if needed, still in the water. Then a floating backboard goes underneath, and the torso and head are secured before the lift. On land, remove wet clothes and cover the patient.
slides.sayZh: 在水中，以下情况要怀疑脊柱损伤：跳水或坠落入水；病人无反应、又无法排除颈部受伤；四肢无力、麻木或瘫痪；或者你拿不准。跳水伤多数伤在颈椎，所以出水之前就要稳住脊柱。病人脸朝下时，救援者把他的整个上半身作为一个整体翻成仰面，而不是只转头。呼吸优先：一翻正，就在水里开放气道，需要就通气。然后把漂浮背板滑到身下，固定好躯干和头部再抬出水面。上岸后脱掉湿衣服、给病人盖好。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: drowning and cold
slides.body:
BC Drowning/Near Drowning and Hypothermia protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Spinal motion restriction if the mechanism suggests it
  • At rest, sitting up; wet clothes off, dry, keep warm
  • Gentle handling; IPPV if breathing is failing
  • Pulse check up to 30–45 s; AED up to 3 shocks
  • Mild/moderate: rewarm; severe (< 28 °C): insulate only

PCP adds

  • CPAP if indicated (age 13+, awake, RR > 24, SpO₂ < 94%)
  • Or a PEEP valve on the BVM: start at 5, max 10 cmH₂O
  • Remove PEEP if systolic < 90 or arrest
  • Hypothermia itself: no PCP-only steps
slides.say: After a cold-water rescue, every level restricts spinal motion if the mechanism suggests it, keeps the patient at rest and sitting up, removes wet clothes, keeps them warm, handles them gently, and ventilates if breathing fails. In hypothermia, take up to thirty to forty-five seconds for the pulse check; in arrest, the AED may shock up to three times. Rewarm mild and moderate cases actively; only insulate severe ones below twenty-eight degrees. The PCP adds positive pressure: CPAP for an awake patient who meets the criteria, or a PEEP valve on the bag, from five up to ten, removed if the systolic drops below ninety.
slides.sayZh: 冷水救援后，各级别都要做的：受伤机制提示时限制脊柱活动；让病人安静休息、坐起；脱掉湿衣服、保暖；搬动要轻；呼吸衰竭时通气。低体温病人检查脉搏可以花三十到四十五秒；心脏骤停时，AED 最多可电击三次。轻度和中度低体温要主动复温，低于二十八度的重度低体温只做保温。PCP 多做的是正压通气：清醒且符合条件的病人用 CPAP，或在球囊面罩上加 PEEP 阀，从五到最高十，收缩压低于九十时移除。

slides.title: Rope rescue and the wilderness
slides.body:
Low angleHigh angle
Slopeunder 45°over 45°
Supportmainly the groundfully on the life-safety rope
  • Rescue basket: at least 6 rescuers; litter carry 6–8
  • Carry longer than about 15–20 min: relay teams
  • Never stand below the patient; watch for falling rock
  • Wilderness = a long evacuation, even near a road
slides.say: Low-angle rope rescue is on slopes under forty-five degrees, where the ground carries most of the weight. High-angle rescue is over forty-five degrees, where everyone depends completely on the life-safety rope. A rescue basket needs at least six rescuers, with extra teams of six for long distances. Never stand below the patient, and watch for falling rock. In the wilderness, evacuation time matters more than distance: a patient a few minutes off the road may still need a long evacuation. A litter carry uses six to eight people, and carries longer than about fifteen to twenty minutes need relay teams.
slides.sayZh: 低角度绳索救援在坡度小于四十五度的地方，大部分重量由地面承担；高角度救援在四十五度以上，所有人完全依赖生命安全绳。救援篮至少要六名救援者，长距离还要另加六人一组轮换。绝不要站在病人下方，当心落石。在野外，撤离时间比距离更重要：离公路只有几分钟路程的病人，也可能需要很长的撤离。担架搬运需要六到八人；要抬超过大约十五到二十分钟的，就要几组人接力。

slides.title: Crush injury: danger at release
slides.body:
Long pressure→no O₂: acid and waste build up→weight lifted→waste and bleeding hit the circulation
  • The weight acts like a tourniquet
  • Numb legs: spinal injury, or simply no blood flow
  • Before release: IV in, vital signs, oxygen, team ready
  • Expect sudden shock when the weight comes off
slides.say: In collapses, trenches and confined spaces, think about crush injury and compartment syndrome. Muscle squeezed for a long time works without oxygen and builds up lactic acid and other waste. While the weight is on, the waste stays trapped; the weight acts like a tourniquet. When it comes off and blood flows back, called reperfusion, the waste rushes into the circulation and hidden bleeding is unmasked, so the patient can crash at that moment. Numb legs under a heavy object may mean no blood flow, not only a spinal cord injury. Prepare before the release: IV in, vital signs taken, oxygen on, team ready. The book's sodium bicarbonate isn't a BC drug.
slides.sayZh: 在坍塌、沟渠和密闭空间救援中，要想到挤压伤和骨筋膜室综合征。肌肉长时间受压，会在没有氧的情况下代谢，积累乳酸和其他废物。重物压着时，废物被困在局部，重物起到止血带的作用。重物一移开、血流恢复，也就是再灌注，废物就涌入循环，隐藏的出血也暴露出来，病人可能就在那一刻崩溃。压在重物下的双腿没有感觉，可能只是没有血流，不一定是脊髓损伤。要在解压之前做好准备：静脉开好、生命体征测好、氧气给上、团队就位。书里的碳酸氢钠不是 BC 的药。

slides.q: A worker's legs have been pinned under a concrete slab for 3 hours. He's alert: HR 108, BP 118/74. The technicians are ready to lift the slab. As the PCP, what's your best preparation?
options: Ask them to lift now and start care once he's free
Start an IV first and be ready for sudden shock
Give sodium bicarbonate before the lift
Give Entonox in the enclosed void while they lift
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A worker's legs have been pinned under a concrete slab for three hours. He's alert, with a heart rate of one hundred eight and a blood pressure of one eighteen over seventy-four. The technicians are ready to lift the slab. What's your best preparation? A, ask them to lift now, and start care once he's free. B, start an IV first and be ready for sudden shock. C, give sodium bicarbonate before the lift. D, give Entonox in the enclosed void while they lift. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名工人的双腿被混凝土板压了三个小时。他清醒，心率一百零八，血压一百一十八比七十四。技术员准备抬起混凝土板。你最好的准备是什么？A 让他们现在就抬，等他解脱后再开始处置；B 先开好静脉，准备应对突发休克；C 抬板前给碳酸氢钠；D 在他们抬板时，在封闭的空隙里给他吸笑气。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Lifting a long crush can cause sudden shock as trapped waste and hidden bleeding reach the circulation. BC's Hypovolemia protocol may be used with a systolic above ninety when shock is anticipated, and entrapment is a time delay, so get the line in first. A wastes your last calm moment. C: sodium bicarbonate is not a BC EMR or PCP drug. D: Entonox is contraindicated in a confined space that can't be ventilated.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。长时间挤压一解除，困住的废物和隐藏的出血进入循环，可能突然休克。BC 低血容量流程在预计会休克时，收缩压高于九十也可以启动，而被困本身就是时间延误，所以要先把静脉开好。A 浪费了你最后的平静时刻。C：碳酸氢钠不是 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 药物。D：笑气禁用于无法通风的密闭空间。

slides.title: Packaging for a long carry
slides.body:
• Wire basket: water, helicopter. Plastic: rubble, ladders, snow
  • Pelvis is secured first; broken pelvis → vacuum mattress
  • Spine: KED, or lift and slide the basket under
  • Narrow passage: KED inside a SKED
  • IV on a pressure infuser, not gravity; secure O₂ and lines
  • Baskets don't insulate: cover the patient, keep IV fluid warm
slides.say: Long carries need careful packaging. Wire-mesh baskets suit water and helicopter work, because water and air pass through; plastic baskets slide better over rubble, ladders and snow. Packaging usually anchors the pelvis first, which is agony with a pelvic fracture, so put that patient in a full-body vacuum mattress and secure the mattress instead. A backboard rarely fits a basket: use a KED, or lift the patient as a unit and slide the basket under. The PCP part: run your IV on a pressure infuser, not gravity, and secure it with the oxygen and every line. Baskets don't insulate, so cover the patient and keep IV fluid warm.
slides.sayZh: 长距离搬运需要仔细包装。钢丝网救援篮适合水域和直升机吊运，因为水和空气能穿过；塑料救援篮在瓦砾、梯子和雪地上更容易滑过。包装通常先固定骨盆，这对骨盆骨折的病人是剧痛，所以先把他固定在全身真空床垫里，再把床垫固定进篮内。背板通常放不进救援篮：用 KED，或者整体抬起病人、把篮子滑到身下。PCP 的部分在这里：静脉输液用加压输液器，不靠重力，并和氧气及所有管路一起固定好。救援篮不保温，所以要给病人盖好，也要给静脉液体保温。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Crush release: line in, vitals taken, team ready first
  • Long rescue: reassess patient and IV every 5–15 minutes
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg up to 2 L; listen to the lungs every 500 mL
  • CPAP: not with vomiting, decreased LOC or systolic < 90
  • Entonox: not in unventilated spaces or decompression illness
  • Cold patients: horizontal, gentle; pulse check up to 30–45 s
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs. Before a crush release, the line is in, the vital signs are taken, and the team knows the plan if the patient crashes. BC's IV maintenance guideline means reassessing the patient and the IV every five to fifteen minutes. If you give boluses, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, listen to the lungs every five hundred, especially after drowning, when the lungs may already be wet. CPAP is not for a patient who's vomiting, has decreased consciousness, or has a systolic under ninety. Entonox is out in an unventilated space or with decompression illness. And handle cold patients flat and gently.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 要注意的事。解除挤压之前：静脉已开好，生命体征已测，团队知道病人崩溃时的计划。按 BC 静脉维护规定，每五到十五分钟复评一次病人和静脉。如果补液，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升听一次肺，溺水后尤其要听，因为肺里可能已经有液体。CPAP 不能用于呕吐、意识下降或收缩压低于九十的病人。在无法通风的空间里或有减压病时不能用笑气。低体温病人要保持水平、轻柔搬动。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Mild 32–35 °C, moderate 28–32 °C: actively rewarm, cab 30 °C
  • Severe (< 28 °C): insulate, gentle handling, no active rewarming
  • Cold arrest: AED up to 3 shocks, then CPR without pauses
  • Drowning: PCP adds PEEP or CPAP if indicated
  • Book's sodium bicarbonate and opioids: not BC EMR/PCP drugs
slides.say: For the BC exam, know BC's hypothermia rules. Mild is thirty-two to thirty-five degrees and moderate is twenty-eight to thirty-two: both get active rewarming, with the ambulance preheated to thirty, hot packs wrapped in towels, and warm blankets. Severe, below twenty-eight, is not actively rewarmed: insulate, keep the ambulance at thirty, and avoid rough handling. In a cold arrest, the AED may shock up to three times; after that, continue CPR without pausing to analyze. For drowning, the PCP adds PEEP or CPAP if indicated. And the book's sodium bicarbonate and opioid painkillers are not BC EMR or PCP drugs.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试方面，要掌握 BC 的低体温规定。轻度是三十二到三十五度，中度是二十八到三十二度，两者都要主动复温：救护车预热到三十度、用毛巾包着的热敷包、温暖的毯子。重度低于二十八度，不做主动复温：保温隔热，救护车保持三十度，避免粗暴搬动。低体温心脏骤停时，AED 最多电击三次，之后继续 CPR，不再暂停分析。溺水病人，PCP 有指征时加用 PEEP 或 CPAP。书里的碳酸氢钠和阿片类镇痛药都不是 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 药物。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Confined space or trench: assume deadly; secure, don't enter
  2. Water: reach, throw, row, go; cold patients flat and gentle
  3. Long rescue: IV before crush release; secure lines; reassess often

Next: Chapter 53, Hazardous Materials Incidents
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: in a confined space or trench, assume the hazard can kill you. Secure the scene, keep everyone out, and call the team with the right equipment; most people who die in confined spaces were trying to help. Two: in water, reach, throw, row, go, and enter only if trained. Handle cold patients flat and gently. Three: long rescues change the PCP's plan. Get the IV in before a crush release, run it on a pressure infuser, secure every line, and reassess every five to fifteen minutes. Next class: Chapter 53, hazardous materials incidents. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，在密闭空间或沟渠，要假定危险能要你的命：控制现场，不让任何人进入，呼叫有合适装备的队伍；密闭空间里死去的人大多是想去救人的人。二，在水域，按「伸、抛、划、游」，只有受过训练才下水；低体温病人要水平、轻柔地搬动。三，长时间救援会改变 PCP 的计划：解除挤压前先开好静脉，用加压输液器，固定好每一条管路，每五到十五分钟复评一次。下节课是第 53 章「危险品事件」。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
